characterList.description: Caucasian male, brown hair, wearing a black suit, white shirt, and blue tie with white stripes.
characterList.name: Maximillian Jacobson-Gonzalez

characterList.description: Black male, black hair, wearing glasses, black suit, white shirt, and tie with black and yellow pattern.
characterList.name: Debrestsion G/Michael

content_metadata.description: An interview conducted by Maximillian Jacobson-Gonzalez with Debrestsion G/Michael, the Minister of MCIT Ethiopia, discussing Ethiopia's digital transformation at the ITU Telecom World 2017.

qAndA.answer: He expresses gratitude and says "Thank you for inviting me, too."
qAndA.question: What was the Minister's response to being invited for the interview?

qAndA.answer: He stresses the significance of "mindset" and "cultural change", highlighting that even with technology, it's crucial to have the right mentality to utilize it effectively.
qAndA.question: What did the Minister describe as being very important for the digital transformation?

qAndA.answer: To showcase Ethiopia's progress in digital transformation, seek partnerships, attract investors in the IT sector, and specifically promote the IT park they have developed for the private sector.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the Ethiopian pavilion at the ITU Telecom World?

qAndA.answer: He cites "health" and "education" as areas that require content development to benefit from the digital infrastructure.
qAndA.question: What specific areas does the Minister mention as needing content development to support digital transformation?

qAndA.answer: They shake hands, signifying the conclusion of a successful interview.
qAndA.question: What gesture do both interviewer and interviewee make at the end of the interview?

characterInteraction.description: The interviewer and the Minister engage in a professional and respectful conversation. The Minister responds thoughtfully to the interviewer's questions, sharing his insights and vision for digital transformation in Ethiopia.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The Minister's emphasis on the need for a "comprehensive approach" highlights the interconnected nature of digital transformation and the importance of engaging all stakeholders. The discussion on affordability underscores the need to bridge the digital divide and ensure equitable access to technology for all citizens.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of the Minister and the setting.
Discussion on digital transformation, its challenges, and opportunities for Ethiopia.
Conclusion of the interview with well wishes for the pavilion.

scenes.thematicElements: Digital transformation in Ethiopia; Challenges of digital transformation in developing countries; The role of education and awareness in digital literacy; The importance of partnerships and investment in the ICT sector.
scenes.title: Interview Scene

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: We're here at ITU Telecom World 2017 in Poussin in the Republic of Korea and I'm very
pleased to be joined in the studio today by the Minister for ICTVth here at the Broad
Sub-Michael Minister, thank you very much for being with us.
Thank you for inviting me to.
Now I'd like to start off by talking to you about the leadership summit where you just
came off the stage from and you just spoke on about visions of smart societies.
Perhaps you could share a little bit about what your vision is with us here.
Of course, well I'm sure very well why we need this digital transformation.
It's about changing the life of our people.
We want to address a number of issues, the development issues on health, education, poverty,
services.
Unless we use digital intervention digital technology, we cannot transform the whole thing.
So this digital intervention is a transformative intervention that makes life easier.
So we have a very comprehensive approach towards it and when we say transformation it's
not just about using IT.
Although IT is the main component of the information technology, you have to change mind of people.
It's about transformation, it's not about just incremental change.
It's about doing things anyway.
So there must be a shift from the traditional way of doing things.
So we have to work on the mind of people.
They just have to understand that they should not do the same thing.
The way they have come all over.
It's a government, the private sector, the citizen, so that's why it is transformative.
Therefore all citizens must be on board.
Government, private sector, everyone.
If you lose anyone of them or even some part of them, then they will not transform.
So we give a lot of importance and weight for digital transformation.
That's why we have to approach it's a very comprehensive approach.
Because itself is a comprehensive change.
It has to be dealt with a comprehensive approach.
So we have a very concerted effort plan that prioritizes the engagement.
They said different sectors, different stakeholders.
So it's about changing the world we live in.
So it is very fast for us when we talk about digital transformation.
And what are the major challenges you think?
Well the main one I was just mentioning about the issues.
One is mindset.
The main set is very important.
If the mindset is not right, then even if you have the technology, you are not going to
use it into good use.
So all of us have to be ready to move from what we are used to do.
So the readiness, it starts from the government again.
The private sector is the citizen.
So the culture change is the most important.
The mindset is the most important.
The readiness to use this technology is the key for us.
There is, well, you have to have the technology.
So connectivity is another very important challenge.
Because we are talking about technology digitalization.
Unless you have this affordable access to everyone, not to people in town.
To remote areas, to all citizens, then there is a digital transformation.
So that's the second one.
Because the investment is about affordability.
Although we have many several technical solutions, are they affordable?
Can people use it?
Special is a poor in the remote areas.
And what about education?
I was going to say what about education?
What role does education play in this?
Education for me is a common denominator in this digital transformation, but also in
others.
That is a key.
Because we have to start with awareness.
As I said, people, the remote area, people at the university, at other places, they have
to be ready to impress this digital revolution.
So at different levels, we need education.
This awareness, meaning just what you call digital literacy.
So that they can easily use whatever technology are available.
This can be mobile.
You don't need to be sophisticated gadgets, but people have to know, at least understand.
So that they have to put it into good use.
At higher levels, and you need programmers, developers, who can develop content for the
people on health education.
So we have this continuum of educational levels that we have to address, meaning different
people.
So we have to have a proper curriculum that addresses all this segment.
Some just awareness sensitization in expertise.
So that we will use this infrastructure for health, for education, and for other purposes,
for government services, for e-commerce.
So we need this top-notch people as well, who can develop this application as different
services.
We need this education.
So the spectrum is so wide.
Now, Ethiopia has a pavilion here.
I wanted to find out what's the value of attending events such as ITU Telecom World,
and have you got a key message here for participants?
Yeah, actually, it is our first time that we are coming to Busan with this pavilion.
So we need to show that we are making some progress.
At the same time, we also want partnership, because when we say there are some progress,
it doesn't mean we are complete.
We show that there are some advancements, but we still need to do much more.
So with this pavilion, we expect one to introduce ourselves, but at the same time, to engage,
to look for partnership, because this is global platform.
So this is for us an opportunity to introduce, as well as to know other companies, this
innovative solution providers.
So this will be an opportunity for bridging the gap.
So I think we can best use this opportunity to identify resources that we can use in our
country.
In some cases, we are also looking for investors on IT, specific on IT, and we have developed
already an IT park for private sector.
So this can be an avenue for anyone who is interested to invest at the same time develop
our IT ecosystem.
So we are looking for partnership.
So we are looking for people or companies innovators who have any interest, who can even start
acquaintance and communication with us, so that they will be part of our development.
That is the main mission of this pavilion.
Great, we wish you the very best of luck, and I'm sure you'll get some interest, and thank
you very much, Diff.
Thank you.
Thank you for inviting me as well.
Thank you.
Thank you.
